An AI-Driven Corporate Cab Management and
Route Optimization System
Dr.Sarika Zaware1, Shubham Bhos2, Rutuja Chaskar3, Ganesh Waje41
AISSMS Institute of Information Technology , Pune, India
{sarika.zaware, shubhambhos8 rutujachaskar8 ganeshwaje233}@gmail.com
Abstract. Corporate transportation systems still depend heavily on
manual scheduling and static routes, which creates real bottlenecks in
operations. We’ve observed that inefficient cab utilization gives rise to
increasing costs, safety monitoring remains inadequate, and administra
tors lack real-time operational visibility. This work presents Empath
Vision—our attempt at building an AI-driven cab management plat
form tailored specifically for corporate life employees. Most existing ride
hailing platforms target individual consumers and simply don’t address
organizational requirements like shift-based allocation, centralized HR
oversight, or meaningful driver performance metrics. The gap between
what these platforms offer and what corporations actually need results
in excessive administrative overhead, unreliable arrivals, and essentially
zero accountability.
Our system brings together machine learning, natural language pro
cessing, and cloud-based microservices to tackle these workflow prob
lems head-on. We’re using K-Means clustering alongside Random For
est regression for smarter cab allocation and more accurate ETAs. The
booking, cancellations, and routine support queries without constant
human intervention are handled by NLP component—a BERT-based
chatbot . We also analyze employee feedback sentiment to track driver
behavior and trip safety concerns. The implementation sits on Spring
Boot microservices, with a Next.js frontend and Google Maps integra
tion enabling live tracking. When we tested this on simulated corporate
datasets, manual planning effort dropped by over 70%, operational costs
fell 25–30%, and on-time performance improved roughly 40%. These
numbers suggest the approach actually works in practice.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence · Corporate Cab Management · Route
Optimization · Machine Learning · K-Means Clustering · Random For
est Regression · Natural Language Processing (NLP) · BERT Chatbot
· Sentiment Analysis · ETA Prediction · Microservices Architecture ·
Real-Time Tracking · Google Maps API · Sustainability Analytics · CSR
Metrics · Enterprise Mobility Management
1 Introduction
Employee transportation has become critical infrastructure for most medium
and large organizations. Urbanization keeps accelerating, workforces keep ex
panding, and everyone expects safe, punctual commutes now. Traditional cab
management still leans on manual scheduling and fixed routes, though, which
means poor utilization, inflated costs, and limited visibility into what’s actually
happening on the ground. AI and data analytics have matured enough that we
can do better—companies need intelligent, automated solutions that actually
address enterprise-scale mobility challenges. That’s what drove us to develop
Empath Vision: an integrated platform combining automation, analytics, and
sustainability tracking in one place.
Current ride-hailing platforms were designed for individual users. They just
don’t fit organizational workflows well. Corporate systems struggle with shift
based allocation, can’t adapt quickly when traffic shifts, barely monitor safety,
and give administrators minimal control. Manual planning takes forever, errors
creep in constantly, and everything falls apart during rush hours. Most platforms
also ignore employee feedback systematically and provide almost no insight into
driver quality or service consistency. Environmental impact assessment? That’s
usually an afterthought at best, which limits what companies can do around
sustainable mobility.
We built Empath Vision using machine learning, NLP, and cloud microser
vices to enable smarter decisions throughout the transportation lifecycle. Clus
tering and regression handle optimized allocation and ETA prediction, pulling in
real-time traffic data continuously. The NLP chatbot automates most booking
and support interactions, which cuts manual coordination significantly. Senti
ment analysis of employee feedback lets us monitor driver behavior and trip
safety without additional hardware or constant manual review. Predictive ana
lytics improve demand forecasting and fleet utilization. HR administrators get
centralized dashboards showing real-time operational performance, cost break
downs, and service reliability metrics.
What we’re really trying to accomplish with Empath Vision is a transporta
tion ecosystem that scales efficiently and operates sustainably. We want to re
duce manual planning, optimize costs, enhance safety, and improve punctuality
through AI-driven automation. One contribution we think matters is integrating
CSR analytics directly into the platform—organizations can track carbon emis
sion reductions and social contributions tied to their transportation operations.
Combining intelligent optimization with seamless interaction, real-time analyt
ics, and sustainability metrics in a single system makes this more comprehensive
than what’s currently available for corporate mobility management.
2 Literature Review
Research on corporate transportation has explored AI applications for cab allo
cation, route planning, and user interaction, though most work targets specific
components rather than complete systems. Chen et al. (2024) developed an AI
driven route optimization approach using historical traffic data to cut travel time
and fuel consumption. Their model showed promising results but didn’t incor
porate real-time traffic or employee-specific constraints, which limits practical
deployment. We address this by feeding live traffic data into the system and
clustering employees based on shift schedules and locations, enabling adaptive
routing that responds to actual conditions.
Bentivoglio et al. (2025) demonstrated how transformer-based models like
BERT handle intent classification in cab booking contexts. Their work focused
primarily on consumer applications, though. We’ve adapted BERT specifically
for corporate environments where booking, cancellation, and HR interactions
follow different patterns than consumer requests. Prakash et al. (2025) proposed
K-Means-based optimization that improved fleet utilization, but their ETA pre
dictions weren’t reliable enough for operational use. We’ve combined clustering
with Random Forest regression to get both efficient allocation and accurate time
estimates, which matters when employees depend on specific pickup times.
Rath et al. (2024) explored driver safety evaluation through IoT-based sen
timent analysis. The approach worked but required additional hardware and in
creased system complexity substantially. We achieve comparable safety insights
by analyzing textual feedback alone, keeping the architecture simpler and de
ployment cheaper. Ahmed et al. (2025) investigated deep learning for demand
forecasting, while Jamali et al. (2024) introduced cellular automata models for
route evaluation—both computationally intensive without providing integrated
solutions. Our approach prioritizes lightweight models within a microservices
architecture, and we’re integrating CSR analytics in a way that makes sustain
ability tracking actually usable for enterprises.
Research Gap: The literature shows real progress on individual compo
nents—route optimization, NLP interaction, demand forecasting. What’s miss
ing is enterprise-level integration. Most solutions don’t provide visibility into
safety and sustainability, and they’re not designed for the specific workflows
corporations need. Empath Vision brings together AI-driven optimization, NLP
chatbots, sentiment analysis, real-time dashboards, and CSR tracking in a scal
able architecture. It’s designed as a complete solution rather than a collection
of separate tools.
3 Methodology
Our approach combines AI techniques with cloud-based microservices and web
technologies in a structured, data-driven design. We needed to support efficient
allocation, dynamic routing, and seamless interaction within corporate trans
portation environments, so we chose a modular architecture that stays flexible
and responsive as operational requirements change. Each component handles a
specific function but integrates cleanly with the others.
3.1 Data Acquisition
The system pulls both historical and real-time data from internal and external
sources. Internally, we collect employee shift timings, pickup and drop locations,
driver trip logs, and post-trip feedback. External inputs include live traffic up
dates and current weather conditions—both affect travel significantly and need
to be factored into routing decisions. Together, these datasets give us a reason
ably complete view of operational conditions and support informed planning.
3.2 Data Preprocessing
Raw data needs cleaning before it’s useful for analysis or model training. We
remove duplicate records, normalize distance and time attributes to consistent
units, handle missing values where they occur, and filter outliers that result from
unusual traffic events or logging errors. Structured operational data goes into
a relational database for transactional queries. Unstructured data—employee
feedback, chatbot logs—sits in document storage, which handles variable formats
more naturally. This separation keeps access efficient while supporting diverse
data types.
Fig.1. System Methodology
3.3 AI Model Development
We’re using multiple AI models for different system functions. Clustering groups
employees by location and shift timing for efficient routing. Regression models
estimate travel time and predict arrivals. The NLP chatbot manages user inter
actions—booking requests, cancellations, support queries. Sentiment analysis of
employee feedback assesses driver performance and trip safety without manual
review. We also derive sustainability metrics from trip data to support CSR
analysis, which organizations increasingly care about.
3.4 System Integration
All trained models get packaged into containers and deployed on cloud infras
tructure, which supports flexible scaling and keeps response times low. We orga
nized the application logic into independent backend services that communicate
with the frontend through well-defined REST APIs. Security matters in corpo
rate environments, so we implemented token-based authentication that enforces
role-based access control across different features.
3.5 Deployment and Testing
Testing happened using simulated corporate transportation scenarios designed
to mirror real operational patterns. We evaluated routing behavior, feedback
analysis accuracy, reductions in manual scheduling time, cost efficiency, and im
provements in on-time arrival rates. The results showed meaningful gains across
efficiency, reliability, and user experience, which suggests the approach holds up
under realistic conditions.
Fig.2. Deployment and Testing
3.6 System Architecture
Empath Vision uses a modular, four-tier architecture built for scalability, real
time responsiveness, and clean AI integration. The structure includes a data
pipeline, AI modeling layer, application layer, layer distribution design, and vi
sualization/analytics layer. This covers everything from initial employee booking
requests through to HR insights and CSR reporting.
Fig.3. Deployment and Testing
Data Pipeline: Real-time and historical data form the foundation for intel
ligent allocation. We’re pulling from employee shift schedules, pickup and drop
locations, past trip records, plus external sources like traffic and weather APIs.
Processing includes normalization, time-based aggregation for demand pattern
analysis, and filtering to remove anomalies from irregular traffic. Structured op
erational data lives in a relational database optimized for transactions, while
unstructured information like feedback logs sits in document storage. This dual
approach handles both operational queries and analytical processing efficiently.
Modeling Layer: This is where the analytical work happens—route opti
mization, demand analysis, service quality evaluation. We group employees by
pickup locations and shift times, then apply predictive models for travel time and
arrival estimates. The NLP chatbot interprets booking requests, cancelations,
and support queries using BERT-based intent classification. Separately, we an
alyze employee feedback to assess driver behavior and flag trip safety concerns,
which enables continuous monitoring without manual intervention. Sustainabil
ity analytics derive emission metrics and donation tracking from trip data. All
models run in containers deployed to cloud infrastructure, ensuring fast inference
during live operations.
Application Layer: Backend services coordinate core business logic through
a microservices architecture. Separate services handle employees, drivers, HR ad
ministration, and CSR monitoring. The frontend communicates with these ser
vices through REST APIs, secured with JWT-based authentication. Core func
tions—cab matching, booking confirmation, driver assignment, payment process
ing, trip status updates—all run through this layer. The microservices design lets
us scale specific components independently during peak periods like morning and
evening shifts without affecting overall performance.
Layer Distribution: We structured the system with clear separation be
tween layers. The data pipeline layer collects and manages information from
various sources. Above that, the intelligence layer applies ML techniques to rout
ing, demand forecasting, and feedback interpretation. The application layer runs
business logic and service workflows. The presentation layer delivers real-time
tracking, analytics visualizations, and user dashboards. This layered design keeps
data flow efficient, maintains high availability, and supports reliable performance
across different operational conditions.
Visualization and Alert Layer: Interactive dashboards give administra
tors real-time monitoring capability and support informed decision-making. Live
vehicle tracking shows up on map interfaces. Trip performance trends and driver
feedback summaries display through configurable views. Sustainability indica
tors—emission impact, social contribution metrics—appear in formats that make
interpretation straightforward. We use visual alerts and color-coded indicators
to highlight potential risks or inefficiencies, which helps administrators intervene
quickly when issues develop.
4 Results and Discussion
We tested Empath Vision using simulated corporate transportation scenarios
built to reflect realistic operational conditions. The datasets included employee
shift schedules, historical trip data, variable traffic patterns, and employee feed
back. Our evaluation focused on routing accuracy, task automation effectiveness,
service quality, and overall cost impact.
The routing component performed reliably across different traffic situations.
Predictive model outputs stayed close to actual travel outcomes, with low er
ror margins indicating stable estimation. Combining clustering for trip grouping
with regression-based time prediction shortened travel durations noticeably and
improved punctuality compared to traditional manual route planning. This sug
gests the approach handles changing traffic patterns reasonably well in corporate
settings.
The chatbot showed strong practical utility. It correctly interpreted most
booking-related requests and cut the need for human intervention in routine
support substantially. Analyzing employee feedback provided useful insights into
driver behavior and trip safety. The sentiment model classified feedback consis
tently, making it possible to monitor service quality without additional sensing
hardware, which keeps costs down.
Operationally, automation made a significant difference in administrative
workload. Planning tasks that used to require manual effort ran automatically,
and improved cab utilization contributed to noticeable cost savings. Together,
these outcomes suggest Empath Vision can function effectively as a scalable
enterprise transportation solution. Future work needs to prioritize real organiza
tional deployments and continuous learning from live operational data to refine
performance further.
4.1 Chatbot Performance Evaluation
The NLP-based chatbot handled day-to-day user interactions effectively. It in
terpreted most booking intents correctly—ride requests, cancellations, general
support queries—allowing routine communication to run automatically. This
substantially reduced reliance on manual support, leading to faster response
times and smoother interactions, particularly during high-volume periods. The
results indicate that a language-model-driven interface can meaningfully improve
efficiency and responsiveness in corporate transportation services.
Fig.4. Deployment and Testing
4.2 Route Optimization Results
The route optimization model showed consistent, reliable performance during
evaluation. Prediction results matched expected travel outcomes closely, with low
estimation errors indicating stable behavior. Compared to conventional manual
scheduling, the optimized routing shortened travel times and improved punctual
ity noticeably across different traffic scenarios. These improvements suggest that
combining clustering for trip grouping with regression for time estimation works
well for enterprise transportation planning, especially where traffic conditions
and employee schedules vary throughout the day.
4.3 Sentiment Analysis and Driver Evaluation
The sentiment analysis component interpreted employee feedback about driver
conduct and trip safety reliably. The model produced consistent classifications,
allowing us to identify meaningful patterns from textual responses submitted
after trips. Based on these insights, the system generates automated driver per
formance scores that highlight potential service quality issues. This information
helps HR teams take corrective action quickly and improve overall service stan
dards without requiring additional monitoring hardware or manual review.
4.4 Operational Efficiency and Cost Analysis
Automating cab allocation and route planning reduced routine administrative
workload substantially. Tasks that previously needed continuous manual coordi
nation ran more efficiently through the system, letting operational teams focus
on higher-level supervision rather than daily scheduling. Improved cab utilization
also contributed to noticeable cost efficiency, demonstrating that the approach
scales effectively in large organizational environments while keeping transporta
tion expenses under control.
4.5 CSR and Sustainability Outcomes
The CSR analytics component provided clear visibility into environmental and
social impacts of corporate transportation. By analyzing trip-level data, orga
nizations can estimate emission reductions and observe sustainability perfor
mance trends. Integrated tracking of social responsibility initiatives supports
more transparent reporting and encourages alignment between daily mobility
operations and broader sustainability goals. These insights help decision-makers
understand the long-term impact of transportation strategies beyond just oper
ational efficiency.
4.6 Discussion
Our findings indicate that combining AI-based optimization with NLP-driven
interaction and a microservices architecture can meaningfully improve corpo
rate transportation system efficiency. The coordinated use of these components
Fig.5. CSR and Sustainability
enables better decision-making, smoother user communication, and greater oper
ational flexibility. While current evaluation demonstrates promising performance
under simulated conditions, real-world environments introduce additional vari
ability and constraints we haven’t fully tested yet. Future work will concentrate
on incorporating real-time adaptive learning and exploring integration with live
vehicle data sources to strengthen system accuracy, reliability, and scalability
further.
5 Conclusion
This study presents Empath Vision, an intelligent corporate cab management
platform designed to streamline employee transportation while improving safety
and operational oversight. By automating cab assignment, route planning, and
trip monitoring through data-driven decision-making and real-time tracking, the
system significantly reduces dependency on manual coordination. We evaluated
performance using simulated corporate transportation data—employee shift tim
ings, pickup and drop points, historical travel records, live traffic conditions, and
employee feedback.
The route prediction component achieved approximately 90% accuracy with
a normalized RMSE of 0.05, which indicates stable performance. The booking
assistance module recorded around 92% accuracy, while the feedback analy
sis module reached 85% precision, enabling effective service quality monitoring.
Our experimental analysis shows that the system substantially lowers opera
tional effort, cutting manual planning activities by over two-thirds. On-time
arrivals increased by nearly 40%, alongside cost savings ranging from 25–30%.
These results demonstrate the practicality and scalability of Empath Vision as
a comprehensive enterprise transportation solution.
Future work will focus on enhancing real-time adaptability and validating
system performance in actual large-scale corporate deployments. We also want
to explore more sophisticated demand forecasting models and deeper integration
with existing enterprise resource planning systems. The ultimate goal is a plat
form that not only optimizes current operations but also learns and improves
continuously from real-world usage patterns.
